description:
The Girl Students Health & Hygiene Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2018. 

This initiative aims to promote health and hygiene among girl students in schools across the country. 

The scheme is particularly focused on ensuring that adolescent girls have access to sanitary napkins. 

The primary objective is to improve menstrual hygiene management among school-going girls. 

The scheme targets girls aged between 10 to 19 years. 

This age group is critical as it encompasses the onset of menstruation for many girls. 

The initiative aims to reduce school dropouts among girls due to menstruation-related issues. 

The government has set a measurable target to provide sanitary napkins to over 1 crore girls annually. 

The scheme aims to ensure that girls have access to sanitary products at an affordable price. 

Under this scheme, the government provides sanitary napkins at a subsidized rate. 

The cost of a pack of sanitary napkins is set at ₹6 for a pack of six napkins. 

This is significantly lower than the market price, which can range from ₹30 to ₹50 for similar products. 

The scheme also includes awareness programs about menstrual hygiene management. 

These programs are conducted in schools to educate girls about the importance of hygiene during menstruation. 

The initiative is implemented through the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 

State governments are responsible for the distribution of sanitary napkins in schools. 

The scheme also aims to create a supportive environment for girls to discuss menstrual health. 

This includes training teachers to address menstrual hygiene issues in schools. 

The application process for schools to participate in the scheme is straightforward. 

Schools must register with the local education department to receive sanitary napkins. 

Required documents include a school registration certificate and a list of enrolled girl students. 

Once registered, schools can place orders for sanitary napkins through designated suppliers. 

The distribution of sanitary napkins is done on a monthly basis to ensure a steady supply. 

Schools are encouraged to conduct awareness sessions at least once a month. 

The frequency of these sessions can vary based on local needs and school schedules. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various states. 

In 2020, the scheme was expanded to include rural areas where access to sanitary products is limited. 

The government has allocated ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2021-2022. 

This funding is aimed at increasing the reach of the program to more schools. 

The scheme also aims to empower girls by promoting their health and well-being. 

By ensuring access to sanitary products, the government aims to reduce stigma associated with menstruation. 

The initiative is part of a broader effort to promote gender equality in education. 

Research indicates that lack of access to menstrual hygiene products can lead to increased absenteeism among girls. 

In some regions, studies have shown that up to 23% of girls miss school during their menstrual cycle. 

The scheme aims to address this issue by providing affordable sanitary napkins. 

The government has also partnered with NGOs to enhance the reach of the program. 

These partnerships help in conducting workshops and awareness campaigns in remote areas. 

The Girl Students Health & Hygiene Scheme is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. 

It specifically contributes to Goal 3 which focuses on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all. 

The scheme has been recognized for its role in reducing health risks associated with poor menstrual hygiene. 

Girls who lack access to sanitary products are at a higher risk of reproductive health issues. 

The initiative also promotes the use of biodegradable sanitary napkins. 

This is an effort to reduce environmental impact and promote sustainability. 

The government encourages manufacturers to produce eco-friendly products under this scheme. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted by the Ministry of Health. 

Regular assessments help in understanding the impact of the scheme on girls' health and education. 

Feedback from schools and students is collected to improve the program. 

The scheme has been instrumental in changing perceptions about menstruation in many communities. 

Awareness campaigns have led to increased discussions about menstrual health. 

The government aims to expand the scheme to cover more states in the coming years. 

The long-term goal is to ensure that every girl student has access to menstrual hygiene products. 

The scheme is a step towards breaking the silence surrounding menstruation in India. 

It empowers girls by providing them with the necessary resources to manage their health. 

The initiative is crucial for building a healthier and more educated female population. 

The government continues to seek partnerships with private sectors to enhance product availability. 

This includes collaborations with local manufacturers to ensure quality and affordability. 

The scheme has also been highlighted in various national and international forums. 

It serves as a model for similar initiatives in other countries. 

The Girl Students Health & Hygiene Scheme represents a significant commitment by the Indian government. 

It addresses a critical aspect of women's health and education. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the lives of millions of girls across India. 

Efforts are ongoing to ensure that the scheme reaches its full potential. 

The government remains dedicated to improving the health and hygiene of girl students. 

This initiative is a vital part of India’s broader strategy to empower women and girls. 

The scheme exemplifies the importance of addressing health issues in education policies. 

Overall, the Girl Students Health & Hygiene Scheme is a comprehensive approach to a pressing issue. 

It combines health education with practical support for girls in schools. 

The initiative is a testament to the government's commitment to gender equality and health. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a more equitable society for future generations.
